key_facts: **Pyogenic granuloma** (lobular capillary haemangioma) is a fast-growing, **bleeding**, red, moist papule: neither pyogenic nor a granuloma.
Grows over weeks, often after minor trauma; fingers, lips, face, gums (pregnancy epulis).
Triggers: pregnancy, isotretinoin, EGFR inhibitors, other drugs.
Curettage and cautery with **histology** is the usual treatment; send all removed tissue.
Amelanotic melanoma can look identical: a bleeding nodule in an adult needs histology.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: A common, benign, rapidly growing vascular tumour of skin and mucosa. The name is a misnomer: it is neither pyogenic nor a granuloma.

sub: Children and young adults; pregnant women (gingiva).

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Reactive proliferation of lobules of capillaries, often after minor trauma. Hormonal (pregnancy, the "granuloma gravidarum" on the gums) and **drug triggers**, which a pharmacist should know:

ul: systemic retinoids (isotretinoin, acitretin)
EGFR inhibitors (cetuximab, erlotinib, gefitinib; around the nail folds)
BRAF/MEK inhibitors
some antiretrovirals (indinavir)
ciclosporin
capecitabine and taxanes
the combined oral contraceptive
Minor injury, hormones (pregnancy), drugs (retinoids, EGFR inhibitors, protease inhibitors).
**"It's an infection"**: it is a benign vascular proliferation; antibiotics do not help.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Pyogenic granuloma is an **exuberant capillary overgrowth** at a site of injury.

mech.t: Minor injury or hormones release angiogenic factors (VEGF).
Capillaries proliferate in lobules, forming a red, friable nodule that bleeds easily.
mech.caption: Pyogenic granuloma: lobules of capillaries with a collarette of epidermis.

mech.t: Epidermis grows around the base forming a collar; the surface often ulcerates.

histo: Lobular capillary proliferation in an oedematous stroma with an epidermal collarette; ulceration common.

ul: A bright red, glistening, friable papule or polyp, 5–10 mm, developing over **weeks** (the 4-week series is in ). It often has a collarette of scale.
**Bleeds profusely with minor trauma.** Fingers, lips, gums, face, eyelid, and nail folds.

sub: Gingival lesions often regress after delivery; treat if bleeding or troublesome.

ul: Clinical plus dermoscopy (red homogeneous areas, white "rail" lines, collarette).
**Histology is mandatory after removal, because amelanotic melanoma can look identical** (see , ).
+ dermoscopy.
**Mandatory** after removal: amelanotic melanoma can look identical.
Retinoids, EGFR / BRAF inhibitors, ciclosporin, pill.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses

ddx.name: Amelanotic nodular melanoma
ddx.f: Adult, non-traumatised site, recurrence, atypical vessels.

blocks: **Amelanotic nodular melanoma** (the critical one; consider in any adult with a "PG" on a non-traumatised site, recurrence, or atypical vessels), SCC/keratoacanthoma, BCC, Kaposi sarcoma, bacillary angiomatosis (HIV), cherry angioma (older, stable), infantile haemangioma (infants), metastasis (kidney, thyroid), and periungual granulation tissue from an ingrown nail.

ul: **Bleeding first aid:** firm pressure for 10–15 minutes; a non-adherent dressing.

**Refer for removal with histology.** Curettage and cautery (shave/curette plus base cautery) is the usual UK primary-care or dermatology approach. It is discussed at knowledge level in the [skin surgery](condition:skin-surgery-preop) notes.
Silver nitrate or cryotherapy alone gives no specimen and recurs more. Only use them where the diagnosis is not in doubt (e.g. a small pregnancy gum lesion, managed by a dentist).
**Drug-induced PG:** discuss with the prescribing specialist before stopping a cancer drug. Topical timolol or potent steroid are sometimes used by specialists for small periungual lesions.
Pregnancy PGs may regress after delivery; manage conservatively unless bleeding.

A **friable, bleeding vascular lesion** that would bleed during shave alone. **C&C removes it and seals the base**, and the curettings go for **histology** (amelanotic melanoma, SCC and Kaposi are the "must-not-miss" mimics; the [skin lumps](condition:dermatofibroma) notes see *Procedures at knowledge level*).

Alternatives: shave + cautery; excision for recurrent lesions (with closure, as course teaching described); silver nitrate or cryotherapy for very small lesions where the diagnosis is certain (no specimen).
**Posterior neck:** superficial procedures are safe. A deeper excision would need awareness of the spinal accessory nerve (see *Consent, complications and anatomical danger zones*).

ladder.t: Refer for **curettage and cautery** (shave / curette + base cautery) **with histology**.

Discuss with the prescribing specialist before stopping a cancer drug; specialists may use topical timolol or potent steroid for small periungual lesions. Isotretinoin nail-fold granulation: **Yellow Card** + liaise with prescriber.
Gum lesions may resolve after birth (dentist-managed).

blocks.title: Prescribing limits and pitfalls
list: **Silver nitrate / cryo alone**: No specimen, more recurrence: only if diagnosis isn’t in doubt.

refer.t: Rapidly growing red nodule in an adult, especially **sole, nail unit or > 50**: histology; suspected cancer pathway if atypical (amelanotic melanoma).
Typical PG: refer for curettage and cautery with histology.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: A rapidly growing red nodule in an adult, especially on the sole, nail unit or in someone over 50: send tissue for histology; refer on a **suspected cancer pathway** if atypical (amelanotic melanoma).
Recurrent bleeding; recurrence after treatment (satellite lesions).
Rarely resolves untreated; treatment is usually curative.

pearls: Recurrence (up to 15%) and satellite lesions happen. Return if it recurs, and do not assume it is benign.
On isotretinoin? PG-like granulation tissue at the nail folds is a known adverse effect. Report it (Yellow Card) and liaise with the prescriber.

quiz.a: Curettage and cautery of the base, with histology.
Systemic retinoids, EGFR / BRAF inhibitors, ciclosporin, some antiretrovirals.
